findings.summary: The public site is hard-coded to a light theme.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture, computed color-scheme is normal, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light dark support at the document root and retint page tokens with color-scheme, light-dark(), or prefers-color-scheme fallbacks.

findings.summary: Motion-heavy media does not adapt to reduced-motion preferences.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the CSS probe found no reduced-motion rule and a scroll animation remained active; the platform probe found 11 autoplaying videos without controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential animation and autoplay in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block, default media to static posters, and provide play/pause controls.

findings.summary: Page and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/source probe found zero view-transition declarations across the loaded public landing surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document or same-document View Transitions for route and major state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Floating promotional UI is manually positioned rather than anchored with resilient fallbacks.
findings.evidence: The online-editor screenshot shows a floating welcome-bonus card overlapping the hero; the CSS probe found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Attach floating cards and menus to their trigger with CSS Anchor Positioning and position-try fallbacks; ensure viewport-edge collision handling.

findings.summary: Load-time consent and promotional overlays obscure primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, editor, AI-tool, resource, and sign-in screenshots show a cookie banner covering a large portion of the first viewport; several content pages also show a welcome-bonus popup.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the consent surface, avoid overlapping promotional popups, preserve content visibility, and make non-modal notices light-dismissable after a user-triggered action.

findings.summary: Overlay UI does not use native dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The loaded page contained no dialog or popover elements and no ARIA dialog, despite presenting modal-like cookie and promotional overlays.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover for transient promotions, with declarative control, light-dismiss, focus management, and accessible names.

findings.summary: The page overflows horizontally at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured 376 px content against a 360 px visual viewport, producing 16 px horizontal overflow on both English and Arabic homepages.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the 376 px minimum/fixed sizing, use intrinsic fluid widths, and constrain all overlays and media to 100% of the visual viewport.

findings.summary: Reusable components rely on viewport styling rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The computed/source probes found zero @container rules and zero elements with a non-normal container-type.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish inline-size containment on reusable cards, navigation groups, and media tiles, then adapt them with container queries.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and several controls are undersized.
findings.evidence: An active-focus probe successfully focused links and buttons but consistently reported outline: none and no focus box-shadow; the menu control measured only 24 by 24 px and many nav targets were 32 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add high-contrast :focus-visible indicators and enlarge touch targets to at least 44 by 44 CSS px without relying on hover.

findings.summary: The advertised free online editor journey requires account creation before the task can begin.
findings.evidence: “Try online for free” and tool CTAs route to a sign-in page whose main message is “Sign up to unlock all features”; no editing surface is available without authentication.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer a bounded guest editing path or state the account requirement before the CTA; defer sign-up until save/export where possible.

findings.summary: Lab Core Web Vitals are poor on mobile.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.3 s, FCP 5.0 s, CLS 0.261, and a performance score of 0.47. A separate trace on a warm desktop-like run was much faster, so the mobile throttled result is the risk signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP element, reduce initial media/script work, reserve late content space, and retest under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Late content and unreserved images cause visible layout shift.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.261 and identified the templates section plus cookie banner fonts as major shift sources; all 34 audited img elements lacked width and height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio on media, reserve banner space, and use metrically compatible font fallbacks.

findings.summary: Initial delivery is dominated by eager third-party media.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 105 requests and 11.63 MB transferred, including 9.17 MB of media; 98 requests and 11.53 MB came from origins other than www.capcut.com. One synchronous parser-inserted head script was confirmed without async/defer.
findings.suggestedFix: Use posters and user-triggered media loading, defer non-critical login/analytics code, reduce origin fan-out, and keep only truly critical parser-blocking work.

findings.summary: The email sign-in field has no accessible label.
findings.evidence: After opening “Continue with email”, the only email input had no associated label and no aria-label, relying solely on placeholder="Enter email".
findings.suggestedFix: Add a visible label explicitly associated with the email input; keep placeholder text supplementary rather than using it as the name.

findings.summary: Focus indication is removed across the navigation and primary controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused dozens of controls while computed outline remained none and box-shadow remained none, making keyboard location imperceptible.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a consistent, high-contrast :focus-visible outline with adequate offset and preserve logical tab order.

findings.summary: The homepage logs network and CORS errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the console-errors audit due to TikTok monitoring CORS failures; the HAR also recorded monitoring failures and a malformed image 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop or correctly configure failing telemetry requests, remove the malformed image URL, and keep production console/network error-free.

findings.summary: Deprecated markup and unload handlers reduce platform resilience.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported unload event listeners, invalid picture/source markup, and BFCache prevention from unload and no-store behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace unload with pagehide/visibilitychange where needed, correct source to use srcset, and remove avoidable BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Generic link text and a non-standard robots directive reduce crawler clarity.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found four links named only “More” and marked robots.txt invalid because of the unknown LLM-Content directive.
findings.suggestedFix: Give links destination-specific names and move the llms.txt pointer to documented discovery conventions without inserting unknown robots directives.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP settings weaken browser-enforced protection.
findings.evidence: Eight cookies were flagged as insecure by the cookie primitive, all used SameSite=None, two fingerprint cookies last 400 days, and CSP permits unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark HTTPS cookies Secure, choose Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential, shorten fingerprint lifetimes, and migrate CSP to nonces/hashes without unsafe directives.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party activity begins before consent.
findings.evidence: Before any consent action, the tracker primitive observed 13 third-party origins including Microsoft Clarity and TikTok monitoring; the HAR counted 98 third-party requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential analytics and fingerprinting behind consent, minimise identifiers and session-wide collection, and consolidate/batch necessary telemetry.

findings.summary: Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HSTS, nosniff and frame protection but found no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Referrer-Policy and an explicit Permissions-Policy allowing only capabilities required by each surface.

findings.summary: Unknown routes dead-end on an infrastructure error page.
findings.evidence: A representative missing route returned a bare “404 Not Found / Guru Meditation / Goofy Deploy Page Server” page with no navigation, explanation, search, or recovery link.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 with navigation, search, preserved context, and a clear route back to the editor or homepage.

findings.summary: Arabic pages omit document language and direction metadata.
findings.evidence: The Arabic resource page rendered Arabic content while html.lang and html.dir were both empty. Its cookie banner remained English, and the page carries substantial physical left/right CSS alongside logical rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="ar" and dir="rtl" at the root for Arabic routes, localise consent UI, and prefer logical properties throughout reusable layouts.

findings.summary: Email validation errors are not programmatically associated with the field.
findings.evidence: Submitting the empty email state showed “Enter a valid email address”, but the field remained validity.valid=true and had no aria-invalid or aria-describedby association.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native required/type validity or aria-invalid after interaction, associate the error with aria-describedby, and announce it in a polite live region.

findings.summary: Autoplay media and third-party bytes are disproportionate for a landing page.
findings.evidence: The load transferred 11.63 MB, 9.17 MB as media and 11.53 MB from third-party origins; 11 video elements autoplayed muted without controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace below-fold autoplay video with responsive posters, load media on intent/visibility, and enforce per-template third-party and media budgets.

findings.summary: Images are not responsively sized or dimensioned.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all 34 images missing dimensions, 24 without srcset, six oversized beyond twice display width, and one below-fold image eagerly loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit responsive srcset/sizes, intrinsic dimensions, modern formats, and lazy loading for below-fold images while preserving LCP priority.

findings.summary: Agent discovery is documented, but product capabilities are not exposed as safe structured tools.
findings.evidence: The site publishes a useful llms.txt and server-rendered content, but loaded source exposed no WebMCP or agentic tool registration for its editing/generation capabilities.
findings.suggestedFix: Pilot narrowly scoped WebMCP/agentic form tools for safe tasks such as project creation or template search, with explicit confirmation for consequential actions.

Improve crawler link labels and robots conventions
